title: {{NAME}} and the Shadow Thief
moral: True courage means helping others, even when you feel small.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a brave young boy with messy brown hair and bright blue eyes, wearing a red cape, a yellow star on his blue shirt, and red sneakers — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} had a secret. Hidden under his bed, wrapped in tissue paper, was a red cape with a golden star.

Every night before bed, {{NAME}} would take it out and hold it up to the moonlight. "One day," he whispered, "I'll be ready to use this."

That evening, something strange happened. When {{NAME}} looked out his window, the streetlights had no shadows beneath them. The whole neighbourhood had gone dark and flat.

Standing at a bedroom window at night, holding a glowing red cape up to the moonlight, eyes wide with wonder. No text, no words, no letters anywhere in the image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} put on his cape. The moment it touched his shoulders, he felt a warm tingle from his toes to his ears.

He took one step — and zoom! He was at the end of the street. Another step — the park! The cape had given him super speed.

"Whoa!" laughed {{NAME}}, skidding to a stop. He looked down. His own shadow was still there, stretching long and steady on the path. Whatever was stealing shadows hadn't found him yet.

pages.content:
In the middle of the park, {{NAME}} found the Shadow Thief — a small, hunched creature made entirely of grey fog, stuffing shadows into a bulging sack.

"Stop!" shouted {{NAME}}.

The creature froze. It turned two pale eyes toward {{NAME}} and let out a low, sad moan. {{NAME}} noticed something then — the creature had no shadow of its own. It was collecting shadows because it was lonely and cold.

"Oh," said {{NAME}} softly. "You just wanted a friend."

pages.content:
{{NAME}} reached into the sack and pulled out the shadows one by one. He walked from garden to garden, tucking each shadow back under the streetlights and flowerpots and fence posts where they belonged.

With every shadow he returned, the neighbourhood glowed a little warmer.

Then {{NAME}} had an idea. He sat beside the Shadow Thief and let the creature borrow his shadow for a little while — just so it could remember what it felt like to have one. The creature let out a sound like a tiny laugh.

pages.content:
By the time {{NAME}} climbed back through his window, every shadow was home. The streets were warm and familiar again.

He folded his cape carefully and slid it back under the bed. He didn't need it to feel like a hero anymore. He already knew he was one — not because of his super speed, but because he had stopped to listen.

{{NAME}} pulled his blanket up to his chin, closed his eyes, and smiled all the way to sleep.
